title: Edit Themes
intro: WordPress’s Theme File Editor edits the PHP, CSS and JavaScript files of the active theme in the browser. Backdrop deliberately has no code editor in the admin interface.
wordpress: A file tree of the theme on the right, a text area on the left, and an “Update File” button that writes straight to the web server.
backdrop: Code is edited on disk, kept in version control and deployed. Nothing in the admin UI writes PHP or template files. Backdrop caches CSS/JS aggregates, so a changed file needs a cache clear to show.

sections.heading: Where theme files are
sections.text: Core themes: core/themes/<name>; contrib and custom themes: themes/<name>. Templates are *.tpl.php files; styles are declared in the theme’s .info file.
